title: Text 2
subtitle: 学术出版与开放获取之争

sentences.en: Scientific publishing has long been a licence to print money.
sentences.zh: 科学出版长期以来一直是一项一本万利的生意。

sentences.en: Scientists need journals in which to publish their research, so they will supply the articles without monetary reward.
sentences.zh: 科学家需要期刊来发表他们的研究成果，因此他们愿意无偿提供文章。

sentences.en: Other scientists perform the specialised work of peer review also for free, because it is a central element in the acquisition of status and the production of scientific knowledge.
sentences.zh: 其他科学家也免费从事同行评审这一专业工作，因为它是获取学术地位和产生科学知识的核心要素。

sentences.en: With the content of papers secured for free, the publisher needs only to find a market for its journal.
sentences.zh: 论文内容可以免费获得，出版商只需为其期刊找到市场即可。

sentences.en: Until this century, university libraries were not very price sensitive.
sentences.zh: 进入本世纪以前，大学图书馆对价格并不十分敏感。

sentences.en: Scientific publishers routinely report profit margins approaching 40% on their operations, at a time when the rest of the publishing industry is in an existential crisis.
sentences.zh: 科学出版商报告的营业利润率经常接近40%，而此时出版业的其他领域正深陷生存危机。

sentences.en: The Dutch giant Elsevier, which claims to publish 25% of the scientific papers produced in the world, made profits of more than £900m last year, while UK universities alone spent more than £210m in 2016 to enable researchers to access their own publicly funded research; both figures seem to rise unstoppably despite increasingly desperate efforts to change them.
sentences.zh: 荷兰出版巨头爱思唯尔声称其发表的科学论文占全球产量的25%，去年利润超过9亿英镑，而仅英国的大学就在2016年花费超过2.1亿英镑，让研究人员得以查阅自己以公共资金资助的研究成果；尽管改变这一局面的努力越来越急切，这两项数字却似乎仍势不可挡地增长。

sentences.en: The most drastic, and thoroughly illegal, reaction has been the emergence of Sci- Hub, a kind of global photocopier for scientific papers, set up in 2012, which now claims to offer access to every paywalled article published since 2015.
sentences.zh: 最激烈、也完全非法的反应是Sci-Hub的出现。这个网站成立于2012年，就像是科学论文的全球复印机，如今声称可以访问2015年以来发表的所有付费文章。

sentences.en: The success of Sci-Hub, which relies on researchers passing on copies they have themselves legally accessed, shows the legal ecosystem has lost legitimacy among its users and must be transformed so that it works for all participants.
sentences.zh: Sci-Hub的成功依赖于研究人员传递他们自己合法获取的论文副本，它的成功表明，合法出版生态系统在用户心中已经失去了合法性，必须进行变革，使其惠及所有参与者。

sentences.en: In Britain the move towards open access publishing has been driven by funding bodies.
sentences.zh: 在英国，向开放获取出版迈进的行动是由资助机构推动的。

sentences.en: In some ways it has been very successful.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来说，这一举措非常成功。

sentences.en: More than half of all British scientific research is now published under open access terms: either freely available from the moment of publication, or paywalled for a year or more so that the publishers can make a profit before being placed on general release.
sentences.zh: 如今，英国超过一半的科学研究成果以开放获取条款发表：要么在发表时即可免费获取，要么先付费订阅一年或更长时间，让出版商赚取利润，然后再公开发布。

sentences.en: Yet the new system has not worked out any cheaper for the universities.
sentences.zh: 然而，对大学来说，这套新制度并没有变得更便宜。

sentences.en: Publishers have responded to the demand that they make their product free to readers by charging their writers fees to cover the costs of preparing an article.
sentences.zh: 出版商对“让读者免费获取其产品”这一要求的回应是，向作者收取费用，以弥补文章编辑准备的成本。
这些费用从大约500英镑到5000美元不等。

sentences.en: A report last year pointed out that the costs both of subscriptions and of these “article preparation costs” had been steadily rising at a rate above inflation.
sentences.zh: 去年的一份报告指出，订阅费用和这些“文章编辑准备费用”一直在以高于通胀率的速度稳步上涨。

sentences.en: In some ways the scientific publishing model resembles the economy of the social internet: labour is provided free in exchange for the hope of status, while huge profits are made by a few big firms who run the market places.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来看，科学出版模式类似于社交互联网的经济模式：人们免费提供劳动，以换取获得地位的希望，而经营这些市场的少数大公司则攫取了巨额利润。

sentences.en: In both cases, we need a rebalancing of power.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，我们都需要重新平衡权力。

questions.stem: Scientific publishing is seen as “a licence to print money” partly because ____

options.A: its funding has enjoyed a steady increase.
options.B: its marketing strategy has been successful.
options.C: its payment for peer review is reduced.

questions.analysis: 根据题干中关键词a licence to print money because ,定位到第一段第二句，其他科学家也免费进行同行评议的专门工作，因为它是获得地位和生产科学知识的核心要素。正确选项D，acquisition原词， for free替换选项中的，cost nothing.

questions.stem: According to Paragraphs 2 and 3, scientific publishers like Elsevier have ____
questions.analysis: 根据题干关键词Elsevier定位到第三段第一句话，The Dutch giant Elsevier, ....made profits of more than 490m last year. while UK universities alone spent more than 210m in 2016,该公司去年利润超过4.9亿英镑 然而仅英国大学在2016年就花费了超过2.1亿英镑。正确选项A 主要依靠大学图书馆 为定位句的同意表达

questions.stem: How does the author feel about the success of Sci-Hub?
questions.analysis: 根据题干中关键词Sci-Hub的成功定位到第四段第二句， The success of Sci- Hub, .... have themselves legally accessed shows the legal ecosystem has lost legitimacy among its users and must be transformed so that it works for all participants这表明法律生态系统在其用户中已经失去了合法性，必须进行改造，以便为所有参与者服务. 可见作者对于Sci- Hub的成功采取否定态度，正确选项B concerned担忧，担心。A relieved宽慰的，C puzzled困惑的属错误选项， D encouraged鼓励的，正反混淆

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraphs 5 and 6 that open access terms ____

options.A: allow publishers some room to make money.
options.B: render publishing much easier for scientists.
options.C: reduce the cost of publication substantially.

questions.analysis: 根据题干关键词open access定位到第四段，最后一句 ...so that the publishers can make a profit before...,合理收取费用是未来出版商能够获利，A选项为同义替换。B render publishing much easier for scientists使发表对科学家来说容易得多 .C reduce the cost of publication substantiality 降低出版成本 D. free universities from financial burdens使大学摆脱财政负担

options.D: The few feed on the many.
